les: Dik lyne, dun lyne en patrone
kaps_punt: Onderwerp 3 (Visuele geletterdheid), Kwartaal 2: Waarneming en bespreking van visuele stimuli soos foto's en werklike voorwerpe om die kunselemente en die kontras en verhoudinge in letterwerk en/of die maak van patrone te identifiseer en te benoem.

items.bewering: Kyk na die letters bo die deure van party winkels of op party plakkate. Iemand het elke letter self geteken en lank aan die vorm gewerk. Sulke getekende letters noem ons letterwerk.
items.blok: Letters wat iemand self geteken het
items.bron: Smashing Magazine, 'Understanding the difference between type and lettering' (2013): lettering is 'the art of drawing letters', 'a specific combination of letterforms crafted for a single use', and outdoor signage (painted signs) and posters are named as typical places it is found. 'party' (some) keeps the shop/poster claim honest; many modern signs are set in fonts instead. https://www.smashingmagazine.com/2013/01/understanding-difference-between-type-and-lettering/

items.bewering: Jy lees die woord en kyk sommer ook na 'n prentjie.
items.blok: Letters wat iemand self geteken het
items.bron: Mapping checked: lettering is display work whose letterforms are drawn for one purpose and is described as 'illustrative lettering' (Smashing Magazine, as above), so reading it as both a word and a picture holds. It does not lead a learner to think ordinary print is a picture, because the block limits it to drawn letters.

items.bewering: Winkelname en plakkate hoort by gewilde kultuur: dinge wat baie mense elke dag sien.
items.blok: Letters wat iemand self geteken het
items.bron: Wikipedia, Popular culture: 'a set of practices, beliefs, artistic output and objects that are dominant or prevalent in a society', which 'permeates the everyday lives of people' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_culture); Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, popular culture: things popular among ordinary people (https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/popular-culture). Advertising and signage are routinely listed as everyday popular/visual culture. Concept correct as a Grade 4 simplification. Note for a person, not a factual fault: the more common Afrikaans term is 'populere kultuur'; whether 'gewilde kultuur' is the house term is a language decision.

items.bewering: Op 'n mat kom dieselfde blokkie of streep oor en oor in 'n gereelde orde voor.
items.bron: J. Paul Getty Museum, Understanding Formal Analysis - Principles of Design: 'Pattern is the repeating of an object or symbol all over the work of art.' https://www.getty.edu/education/teachers/building_lessons/principles_design.pdf. Read as the patterned example mat that the block returns to ('soos daardie mat'), not a claim about every mat.

items.bewering: Die patroon is daardie gereelde orde en nie die blokkie self nie.
items.bron: Getty (as above): pattern is the repeating of an object all over the work, i.e. the arrangement, not the object. Getty Art & Architecture Thesaurus usage separates 'motifs' (distinct design elements occurring singly) from 'patterns' (designs composed of repeated or combined motifs), e.g. via https://vocabularios.eca.usp.br/vcaa/index.php?tema=4750.

items.bewering: Jy sien so 'n patroon ook op 'n hek en op 'n hemp.
items.bron: Getty pattern definition (as above) applied to everyday objects: gates with repeated bars and printed or woven shirt fabrics carry repeated units in a regular order. Phrased as 'can be seen', not as every gate or shirt.

items.bewering: Ons kyk hierdie kwartaal na foto's en regte voorwerpe soos daardie mat.
items.bron: DBE CAPS Life Skills Gr 4-6, Visual Arts, Grade 4 Term 2, Topic 3 Visual literacy (printed p. 45): 'Observe and discuss visual stimuli like photographs and real objects to identify and name all art elements in lettering and/or pattern-making.' https://www.education.gov.za/Portals/0/CD/National%20Curriculum%20Statements%20and%20Vocational/CAPS%20IP%20%20LIFE%20SKILLS%20GR%204-6%20%20WEB.pdf

items.bewering: 'n Lyn is 'n rand of merk wat jou oog van punt tot punt lei.
items.bron: Getty, Elements of Art: 'Line is a mark with greater length than width' (https://www.getty.edu/education/teachers/building_lessons/elements_art.pdf); Smithsonian Folkways worksheet: 'line: the path of a moving point; line defines edges of shapes and forms' (https://folkways-media.si.edu/docs/folkways/lessons/SFLN012_WS01_Elements_of_art.pdf); Getty Principles: movement 'is the path the viewer's eye takes ... directed along lines, edges'. Mark, edge and eye-leading are all supported.

items.bewering: Skryf dieselfde letter S met 'n dun pen en dan weer met 'n dik kwas. Die dik een lyk swaar, en die dun een lyk lig.
items.bron: Line weight: thicker lines read as heavier and thinner as lighter (Proko, How to draw with line weight, https://proko.com/course-lesson/how-to-draw-with-line-weight/notes; Open College of the Arts, Six examples of why line weights matter, https://www.oca.ac.uk/?p=61181). Mapping checked: 'swaar/lig' is visual weight, which the sentence frames as how it looks ('lyk'), so it does not suggest the ink weighs more.

items.bewering: 'n Lyn kan reguit loop of soos 'n haak krul.
items.bron: Getty, Elements of Art: lines can be 'straight or curved; thick or thin'. The hook comparison only describes a curve shape; mapping holds.

items.bewering: 'n Vorm is 'n plat area binne 'n rand.
items.blok: Die vorm van die letter en die oop ruimte
items.bron: Getty, Elements of Art: 'Shapes are flat and can express length and width'; Folkways: 'shape: area enclosed by line; it is 2-dimensional'; Western Australia SCSA visual art elements glossary: 'A shape is 2D, having height and width.' Correct for shape (the 2D element).

items.bewering: 'n Rooi kol verf op wit papier is 'n vorm. Daar maak die kleur self die rand sonder 'n getekende lyn.
items.blok: Die vorm van die letter en die oop ruimte
items.bron: Arkansas Museum of Fine Arts elements-of-art guide (search extract): shape is an area defined by a line, color or value change; Getty Principles: the eye is directed 'along lines, edges, shape, and color'. A colour boundary without an outline makes a shape.

items.bewering: Die dik letter S se eie lyf is ook 'n vorm.
items.blok: Die vorm van die letter en die oop ruimte
items.bron: Getty: 'Shape is a closed line'; a thick stroke is a flat area bounded by its outline, i.e. a positive shape. Follows from the confirmed definitions above.

items.bewering: Die lyn van 'n hoofletter O maak heeltemal toe. Die oop ruimte binne daardie letter is dus self 'n vorm.
items.blok: Die vorm van die letter en die oop ruimte
items.bron: Wikipedia, Counter (typography): a counter is 'the area of a letter that is entirely or partially enclosed'; O has a closed counter (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counter_(typography)); NIST OSAC lexicon gives O as the example of an enclosed counter. Getty: 'negative space has shape'.

items.bewering: Die oop ruimte rondom die letter is ook 'n vorm.
items.blok: Die vorm van die letter en die oop ruimte
items.bron: Getty, Elements of Art: 'The space around objects is often called negative space; negative space has shape.' Wikipedia, Negative space: the empty space around and between the subject(s) of an image.

items.bewering: In 'n patroon word dieselfde vorm oor die hele mat herhaal. Die herhaling laat jou oog van vorm na vorm aanbeweeg.
items.blok: Die vorm van die letter en die oop ruimte
items.bron: Getty Principles: pattern is repeating 'all over the work of art'; 'Rhythm is created when one or more elements of design are used repeatedly to create a feeling of organized movement'; movement is 'the path the viewer's eye takes through the work'. The sentence does not say only shapes can be repeated, so it does not contradict the line/colour repetition named later.

items.bewering: Kontras is 'n duidelike verskil tussen twee dinge wat langs mekaar staan.
items.blok: Kontras: die duidelike verskil langs mekaar
items.bron: The Art of Education University principles poster (search extract): 'Contrast is the difference between elements in a composition ... value change, size difference'; design course material: contrast refers to how different elements are, 'particularly adjacent elements'; Getty Principles (emphasis): an area stands out 'by contrasting it with other areas ... different in size, color, texture, shape'. 'Duidelike' leaves out subtle contrast, an acceptable Grade 4 narrowing.

items.bewering: Sit 'n dik letter langs 'n dun letter en kyk wat gebeur.
items.blok: Kontras: die duidelike verskil langs mekaar
items.bron: Thick next to thin is a difference in line weight between adjacent elements, which fits the contrast definitions above (difference between adjacent elements, e.g. size).

items.bewering: By baie woorde staan een groot hoofletter voor 'n ry klein letters.
items.blok: Kontras: die duidelike verskil langs mekaar
items.bron: Wikipedia, X-height: lowercase letters are measured to the x-height, capitals to the higher cap height, so a capital is taller than the lowercase letters after it (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-height). Names and sentence-initial words start with a capital, so 'baie woorde' (many words, not all) holds.

items.bewering: 'n Donker vorm op 'n ligte agtergrond wys dieselfde skerp verskil.
items.blok: Kontras: die duidelike verskil langs mekaar
items.bron: Value contrast: Getty, Elements of Art (value = how light or dark); LibreTexts, A World Perspective of Art Appreciation 1.06: black and white is a stark example of contrast (https://human.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Art/A_World_Perspective_of_Art_Appreciation_(Gustlin_and_Gustlin)/01%3A_A_World_Perspective_of_Art_Appreciation/1.06%3A_What_Are_the_Elements_of_Art_and_the_Principles_of_Art). 'Dieselfde' reads as 'likewise a sharp difference', not the same kind of difference as size.

items.bewering: Die eerste letter van 'n woord kan twee keer so hoog wees as die res.
items.blok: Verhouding: een deel teenoor die res
items.bron: Wikipedia, Initial (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial) and Helio drop-cap definition: an enlarged first letter usually two or more lines tall. 'Kan' (can) is correct. In ordinary type a capital is about 1.4 to 1.6 times the x-height, not double (X-height sources above), so the sentence would be wrong without 'kan'; it is right as written.

items.bewering: Verhouding is hoe groot een deel van 'n ding is in vergelyking met die res daarvan.
items.blok: Verhouding: een deel teenoor die res
items.bron: Getty Principles: proportion is how parts (sizes, amounts or number) relate to each other; 'when drawing the human figure, proportion can refer to the size of the head compared to the rest of the body'. Matches the part-to-the-rest wording. It defines proportion, not scale.

items.bewering: In 'n patroon kan die middel van 'n blom groter wees as sy blomblare.
items.blok: Verhouding: een deel teenoor die res
items.bron: A possibility ('kan') about a drawn flower motif; it illustrates the Getty proportion definition (one part compared to the rest). Nothing false is implied about real flowers, and it holds for some real ones (e.g. the sunflower's large centre disc).

items.bewering: Soek eers die dikste en die dunste lyn.
items.bron: A viewing instruction, not a claim about the world: the learner finds the extremes of line weight in the stimulus. Consistent with the line-weight sources above. No 'first', 'oldest' or 'biggest' claim to establish.

items.bewering: Kyk daarna waar twee dele die duidelikste verskil.
items.bron: A viewing instruction. Looking for the strongest difference is looking for the strongest contrast, which fits the contrast definitions above (Art of Education; Getty Principles, emphasis by contrast).

items.bewering: Lyn en vorm is twee van die kunselemente wat jy hier benoem.
items.bron: DBE CAPS Life Skills Gr 4-6, Grade 4 Term 2, Topic 1 (printed p. 45): 'Art elements: line, shape, colour used in own lettering and/or pattern-making'; Getty, Elements of Art lists line and shape.

items.bewering: Kontras en verhouding is die twee ontwerpbeginsels van hierdie kwartaal.
items.bron: DBE CAPS Life Skills Gr 4-6, Grade 4 Term 2 (printed p. 45): Topic 3 'identify and name contrast and proportion in lettering and/or pattern-making'; Topic 1 'Design principles: contrast'; Topic 2 'Design principles: introduce proportion'. No other design principle is named for that term. Both are design principles (Getty Principles lists proportion; contrast is a standard principle).

items.bewering: Met hierdie manier van kyk en hierdie name beskryf jy ook jou eie prent of model en 'n maat s'n.
items.bron: DBE CAPS Gr 4 Term 2, Topic 3: 'Apply learning to own work'; Topic 2 of that term is a 3D mobile or stabile, so 'model' fits. CAPS names 'shape/form' for the 3D work; the lesson's 'vorm' is defined as the flat element, which still applies to a cut-out mobile, and the sentence claims nothing false.

items.bewering: letterwerk: Letters wat iemand self teken sodat die vorm ook iets sê.
items.bron: Read alone and in its block. Smashing Magazine (as above): lettering is the art of drawing letters, letterforms crafted for a single use and purpose. That the drawn form carries meaning fits illustrative and display lettering.

items.bewering: gewilde kultuur: Die alledaagse prente, letters en dinge wat baie mense ken en sien.
items.bron: Read alone and in its block. Wikipedia, Popular culture, and Oxford Learner's Dictionaries (as above): the artistic output and objects prevalent in a society and widely known among ordinary people. 'Dinge' is broad enough to cover music, TV and so on, so the entry is a fair simplification, not a narrowing into falsehood.

items.bewering: patroon: 'n Gereelde orde waarin iets oor en oor herhaal word.
items.bron: Read alone and in its block. Getty Principles: 'Pattern is the repeating of an object or symbol all over the work of art.'

items.bewering: lyn: 'n Rand of merk wat jou oog van punt tot punt lei.
items.bron: Read alone and in its block. Same sources as the study sentence: Getty (mark), Folkways (line defines edges), Getty Principles (the eye is directed along lines and edges).

items.bewering: vorm: 'n Plat area binne 'n rand. 'n Lyn of 'n ander kleur kan daardie rand maak.
items.bron: Read alone and in its block. Getty and SCSA WA: shape is flat (2D); Arkansas Museum of Fine Arts guide: shape can be defined by a line, colour or value change. Correct for shape. Scope note for a person, not a fault: in Afrikaans 'vorm' also names 3D form, which CAPS uses for Grade 4 models (shape/form), so a later 3D lesson must not reuse this wording as the whole meaning of 'vorm'.

items.bewering: kontras: 'n Duidelike verskil tussen twee dinge wat langs mekaar staan.
items.bron: Read alone and in its block. Same as the study definition: Art of Education University poster; design course material ('particularly adjacent elements').

items.bewering: verhouding: Hoe groot een deel van 'n ding is in vergelyking met die res daarvan.
items.bron: Read alone and in its block. Getty Principles: proportion, e.g. the size of the head compared to the rest of the body.

items.bewering: kunselemente: Die dele waaruit 'n prent gemaak is, soos lyn, vorm en kleur.
items.bron: Read alone and in its block. Getty, Elements of Art: 'The elements of art are the building blocks used by artists to create a work of art' (line, shape, form, space, colour, texture); CAPS Gr 4 Term 2 names line, shape and colour.

items.bewering: ontwerpbeginsel: 'n Manier waarop die dele van 'n prent saamgesit word.
items.bron: Read alone and in its block. Getty, Principles of Design: 'The principles of design describe the ways that artists use the elements of art in a work of art.'

opsomming: Every checkable claim was found true against CAPS (DBE Gr 4 Term 2), the Getty Museum's elements and principles sheets and typography references, and the glossary entries hold when read alone. A person may want to look at two things that are not faults: whether 'gewilde kultuur' is the house term (the more common Afrikaans term is 'populere kultuur'), and that 'vorm' is defined only as the flat element, while Afrikaans and CAPS also use it for 3D form in later model work.
